what: A background-colored curtain covers the hero and the logo in the center starts drawing at .8s (fx:play — the logo Lottie or SVG plays here). At 2.9s a round hole at the center of the curtain grows from 0 to beyond the screen diagonal (150vmax) over 1s power1.out, revealing the photo hero below as a circle (fx:open), and once fully open the curtain is removed (fx:done — the header items’ drop-in from 30% above runs here). On a return visit in the same session the curtain just lifts away at .5s

options.at: Time the hole starts to open (sec), default 2.9 — fx:open fires then
options.dur: Time for all holes to open (sec), default 1 — 0 means immediate
options.size: Fully open hole diameter (CSS length), default 150vmax — original is 150vw on desktop, 150vh on phone
options.once: Give a name and it opens once per session, then a .5s fade from then on — original opAnimationPlayed
options.[data-fx-part=figure]: Center logo slot (optional) — disappears out of the hole along with the curtain
options.fx:play·fx:open·fx:done: Event bubbling up from the curtain element (bubbles)
options.from: Hole starting diameter (CSS length), default 0px — nii-photo 30vw
options.dip: Diameter (CSS length) that briefly shrinks before opening. When given, separate curves apply to the two segments from → dip → size (CSS keyframe style) — nii-photo 18vw
options.dip-at: Share of the shrink phase (0 to 1), default .14
options.lock: If false, scroll is not locked while opening (nii-photo)
options.--fx-fill: Cover color (via style), default var(--kf-surface) — Brand uses var(--kf-accent)

from.where: index.html .sn-op (opening curtain for first visit) — original .l-op mask-size 0 0 → 150vw circle (fv_op_mask)

index.html .np-v-mask — the circular hole in the orange cover goes 30vw → 18vw (14%) → 220vw after .2s, 1.4s cubic-bezier(.25,1,.5,1). Usage type: data-fx-hole-open-intro="at: .2; dur: 1.4; from: 30vw; dip: 18vw; size: 220vw; ease: 0.25,1,0.5,1; play: 0; lock: false" style="--fx-fill: var(--kf-accent)"

note: Blocks document scrolling meanwhile. The circle is two CSS mask layers (panel − circle) so the logo inside the film is cut out too — same as the original.
